tagline: The Eagles beat the Colts 48-10 in Super Bowl CLIII for a fourth straight title, the Cowboys end a 49-game winning streak, and Ryland Maxwell catches a record 53 touchdown passes on his way to a first MVP.

articles.headline: Four in a Row, and Maxwell Runs the Gauntlet: Eagles Rout the Colts 48-10
articles.dek: Philadelphia went 15-2, saw a 49-game winning streak end in Dallas, then won Super Bowl CLIII at home. Ryland Maxwell's first MVP completed a full set of offensive awards.
body: Dorren Skura's Eagles are champions for the fourth season running. Philadelphia beat the Colts 48-10 in Super Bowl CLIII, the 153rd edition of the game, at home, two seasons after beating the same club 30-21 in Super Bowl CLI. The 38-point margin was the widest of the Eagles' season.

The streak is over, though. Philadelphia had not lost since week 5 of Y92 when it went to Dallas in week 16 and fell 35-32, ending a run of 49 straight wins by Skura's club with two Super Bowls inside it. The Cowboys won again in Philadelphia two weeks later, 26-24. Those were the only defeats of the year.

Otherwise the standard held. The Eagles allowed 402 points, the fewest in the league, scored 602, behind only Pittsburgh's 628, and finished first in the power rankings with a point differential of 200. They went 8-1 on the road and 9-2 against clubs with winning records.

The playoffs belonged to them. The Lions fell 48-26 in the divisional round and the Packers 32-19 in the conference final. Then Indianapolis arrived with a 13-4 record and the league's leading rusher, River Kuechly, and scored only 10.

The biggest individual story belonged to Ryland Maxwell, "Mad Max". He caught 53 touchdown passes, a record, and was named Most Valuable Player for the first time. That made him the first player on file to win every award an offensive player can win: 11 rings, 3 Offensive Player of the Year awards, 5 Super Bowl MVPs and an Offensive Rookie of the Year award to go with the MVP. Call it running the Gauntlet. Bones Crawford, "The Doctor", was Super Bowl MVP for the 2nd time after throwing 68 touchdown passes.

articles.headline: Mad Max Catches 53 Touchdown Passes, Wins His First MVP and Completes the Gauntlet
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,692 yards and caught 71 passes in 19 games, 53 of them for touchdowns, and passed God Johnson on the Career Legacy list.
body: For years Ryland Maxwell has been the league's most feared runner. In Y94 he became its most dangerous receiver as well. Maxwell caught 71 passes for only 391 yards, 5.5 a catch, and 53 of them went for touchdowns. That broke the season mark on Skura's record board, which God Johnson had held since Y63.

He still ran the ball. Maxwell added 1,692 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns, and injury cost him 1 of Philadelphia's 20 games. The league named him Most Valuable Player for the first time in his career, ahead of his own quarterback and his 68 touchdown passes. It was the one major award an offensive player can win that he had never won; no player on file had collected all of them before.

His career rushing total reached 27,393 yards, 2,886 more than Lane McCoy, and his 366 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board. His Career Legacy rose from 11,965 to 13,107, past God Johnson's 12,655, and only Sherman Brandson, at 13,488, rates higher. He has 11 rings, every one won with Skura, and his card is now worth 39,532.

articles.headline: The Doctor Throws 68 Touchdown Passes and Is Super Bowl MVP Again
articles.dek: Bones Crawford threw for 5,131 yards and won his sixth ring. He also threw 20 interceptions, the most in the league.
body: Bones Crawford played all 20 of Philadelphia's games for the second straight season and threw 68 touchdown passes, 4 more than in his MVP season a year earlier. He threw for 5,131 yards and ran for 14 more scores, and his 3.4 touchdown passes a game led the league by a distance: Solomon Toohill of the Packers was next with 44.

There was a cost. Crawford threw 20 interceptions, more than twice as many as any other passer; Lukas Samuels of the Cardinals was next with 8. It did not matter in the Super Bowl, where Crawford was named MVP for the 2nd time as the Eagles scored 48.

Most of the touchdowns had one destination. Of his 68 scoring passes, 53 went to Ryland Maxwell and 15 to everyone else. Crawford's overall rose from 86 to 91, his Career Legacy from 8,158 to 8,987, and his card's value by 162%. He has 6 rings, every one won with the Eagles.

articles.headline: Dallas Ends the Streak at 49, Then Beats the Eagles Again
articles.dek: The Cowboys won 35-32 at home in week 16 and 26-24 in Philadelphia in week 18. The Giants lost twice more.
body: The Cowboys had not been much of a problem. In the six seasons since Skura arrived in Philadelphia they had beaten his Eagles once. Then Dallas did it twice in three weeks. In week 16 the Cowboys won 35-32 at home and ended a winning streak that had run since early in Y92: 49 straight wins, two Super Bowls inside it. In week 18 they came to Philadelphia and won 26-24, the only home defeat of the Eagles' season.

Dallas finished only 9-8, against the hardest schedule in the league by strength of schedule, and still beat the champions twice. Lewis Pettis led the league with 6 interceptions, and Taco Coulter caught 14 touchdown passes, more than any other receiver.

The Giants could not do the same. Philadelphia won 24-17 in New York in week 8 and 46-27 at home in week 15. Ty Lock, who played his 300th game this season, threw 22 touchdown passes for a 9-8 club, and New York still had not beaten the Eagles since Y88.

articles.headline: Viennes Repeats as Offensive Player of the Year, With Wingo 47 Yards Behind
articles.dek: Keenan Viennes caught 99 passes for 2,041 yards and Calvin Wingo II 98 for 1,994. Nobody else in the league came close.
body: For the second year running the league's two most productive receivers wore the same uniform. Keenan Viennes caught 99 passes for 2,041 yards in 20 games and was named Offensive Player of the Year for the 2nd time. Calvin Wingo II caught 98 for 1,994. The next receiver on the list, Taco Coulter of the Cowboys, had 1,036.

What neither of them did much of was score. With Ryland Maxwell catching 53 touchdown passes out of the backfield, Viennes finished with 8 touchdown catches and Wingo with 7, down from 29 and 19 a year earlier.
The market did not mind. Wingo's overall rose from 86 to 91 and his card's value by 163.6%. Viennes went from 73 to 79, and his card, priced at 49 a year ago, now sells for 160.

articles.headline: Akiem Brock Makes 75 Blocks, Twice as Many as Anyone Else
articles.dek: The Eagles lineman's card tripled in value. Snoop Dotson and Jacob Proise rose with him.
body: Every Eagles touchdown started somewhere, and in Y94 it usually started with Akiem Brock. The lineman made 75 blocks in 20 games; Cethan Qualls of the Ravens was second in the league with 37. Brock's overall rose from 94 to 98, his Career Legacy passed 10,000, and his card's value rose 201.5% to 25,260.

Snoop Dotson had 3 sacks, tied for the most in the league, with 81 tackles, 2 interceptions and a forced fumble, and his overall climbed from 88 to 93. Tight end Jacob Proise caught 42 passes for 760 yards, and his card rose 256.2%, the biggest gain among the market's established cards. In the secondary Quincy Booker intercepted 4 passes and Koa Zuber, "Uber Feasts", made 144 tackles.

articles.headline: The Colts Reach a Second Super Bowl in Three Years and Lose to Philadelphia Again
articles.dek: Indianapolis went 13-4 behind River Kuechly's 1,825 rushing yards and 35 touchdowns, then scored 10 in the final.
body: Indianapolis has now met Skura's Eagles in two of the last three Super Bowls and lost both, 30-21 in Y92 and 48-10 in Y94. The first time, Dwayne Skura was on the Colts' sideline, a season after winning a ring in Philadelphia. This time he had retired, and the Colts arrived with a new core.

River Kuechly led the league with 1,825 rushing yards and 35 rushing touchdowns in 21 games, and caught just 1 pass. Korey Friend threw for 4,420 yards and 36 touchdowns with 3 interceptions. Reggie Deayon, a rookie defensive back, made 228 tackles and intercepted 5 passes, tied for the second most in the league.

The Colts finished 13-4 and fourth in the power rankings. Kuechly's overall climbed from 71 to 72 and his card still sells for 49. They have the pieces. They do not yet have an answer for Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Atwell Closes to 126 Tackles of the Record, and Spector Passes 400
articles.dek: Kyron Atwell is chasing K'Lavon Settle's 3,185. Siran Spector moved to fourth on the career rushing touchdowns list. Odell Hainsey retired 2 interceptions short.
body: Kyron Atwell made 206 tackles for the Jets in 17 games and reached 3,059 for his career. Only two players have more: Terron Stidham with 3,132 and K'Lavon Settle, whose 3,185 are the league record. Atwell is 73 behind Stidham and 126 behind Settle, one ordinary season away from both.

Siran Spector ran for 29 touchdowns for the Texans and finished the season with 402, past 400 and past Trequan Jensen and Rondale Ikarras. Ahead of him now are Danny Diggs with 408, Tim Wright with 417 and Lane McCoy's record 458.

Two chases stalled. Odell Hainsey retired after Y93 with 41 interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs's record 43, and 2,989 tackles. Deshone Bello of the Jets did not record a sack in 17 games and stays at 23, 1 behind Kalif Suh.

articles.headline: Lazard's Touchdowns Fall From 39 to 18, and Cincinnati Falls to 6-11
articles.dek: Alshon Lazard played every game again, but the Bengals dropped from second in the power rankings to 27th.
body: A year ago Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes as a rookie and the Bengals went 14-3. In his second season he played all 17 games and threw for 3,203 yards with only 3 interceptions, but he finished with 18 touchdown passes. Cincinnati went 6-11 and allowed 594 points.

The ratings moved with the results. The market's skill score for Lazard fell from 91 to 84, his overall rose only from 63 to 64, and his card slipped from 16 to 15. Grover Calitro ran for 1,569 yards for the Bengals, but Cincinnati scored just 435 points, among the fewest in the league.
A Rookie of the Year season is not a promise. Lazard still has time to become the quarterback his first year suggested. After Y94, he no longer has the benefit of the doubt.

articles.headline: Fox, Hainsey and Dwayne Skura Lead a Long Retirement List
articles.dek: Tevin Fox leaves with 69,973 passing yards and no ring. Dwayne Skura leaves with 4 rings and a Defensive Player of the Year award.
body: Tevin Fox played 403 games, threw for 69,973 yards and 618 touchdowns, and never won a ring. He went through his final season, Y93, without throwing an interception. Odell Hainsey retired with 2,989 tackles and 41 interceptions, the third most on file.

Dwayne Skura won 4 rings and was Defensive Player of the Year in his first season after Philadelphia traded him to the Colts. He retires with 1,595 tackles and 21 interceptions. Trequan Roberts, who spent Y93 with the 3-14 Saints, leaves with 3 rings and 1,949 tackles.

The defensive side lost the most. Oli Alaka retires with 2,851 tackles and 38 interceptions, Linval Laulile, a former Defensive Player of the Year, with 2,765 tackles, and defensive lineman Dallin Santoso with 1,355 tackles and 12 sacks.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
body: Abraham Jack of the 13-4 Bills was Defensive Player of the Year with 211 tackles and 3 interceptions. DQ Watts of the Texans made 255, the most in the league.
The 2-15 Titans beat the 10-6-1 Ravens 42-26 in week 5, the upset of the season, and went 0-8 on the road while allowing 657 points.
The Patriots beat the Broncos 68-23 in week 3, and the Dolphins won 61-50 at Carolina in week 9, 111 points in all.
The Chiefs tied twice, 40-40 at Miami and 41-41 at Baltimore, and finished 9-6-2.
The Steelers scored 628 points, the most in the league, and went 13-4.
Kaulani Rahman caught 43 passes for 268 yards in 17 games for the 8-9 Rams.
Rookie quarterback Olivier Slade threw 25 touchdown passes and 4 interceptions for the 4-12-1 Panthers.

didYouKnow.text: Ryland Maxwell is the first player on file with every award an offensive player can win: a ring, MVP, Offensive Player of the Year, Super Bowl MVP and Offensive Rookie of the Year. The MVP came last, in Y94.
Ryland Maxwell averaged 5.5 yards a catch in Y94 and scored on 53 of his 71 receptions.
Of Bones Crawford's 68 touchdown passes in Y94, 53 went to Ryland Maxwell. Keenan Viennes and Calvin Wingo II, the league's top two receivers by yards, caught 15 between them.
